subject: 5-Bullet Friday — A+ Movies, Heresies, Sharpening Your Brain, Videos That Make You Safer, and More

bullets.title: Eat Drink Man Woman
bullets.note:
I've seen this movie at least five times over the past 25 years. It’s a wonderful, feel-good movie, and it will make you \*very\* hungry. For the film nerds, it’s one of the early [Ang Lee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Lee) films (before _Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon_; _Brokeback Mountain_; _Life of Pi_, etc.) that put him on the global map. For the language nerds, you’ll hear many different flavors of Mandarin, plus one showcase of Taiwanese.  
​  
From the description: “Master Chef Chu ([Sihung Lung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sihung_Lung)) is semi-retired and lives at home with his three unmarried daughters, Jia-Jen ([Kuei-Mei Yang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yang_Kuei-mei)), a religious chemistry teacher; Jia-Chien ([Chien-Lien Wu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacklyn_Wu)), an airline executive; and Jia-Ning ([Yu-Wen Wang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wang_Yu-wen_(Taiwanese_actress))), an employee at a fast-food joint. Life at the family’s house revolves heavily around preparing and eating an elaborate dinner every Sunday. The stability of these meals gives them all strength as they deal with new romantic relationships and disappointments.” [You can watch the film for free](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_MQODtUW8k0&rco=1) on YouTube.

bullets.title: Some Contemporary Heresies
bullets.creator: Kevin Kelly
bullets.note:
. Having known Kevin a long time, I suspect that these are collected from some very smart people. Smart doesn’t always equal right, but it does add a little color to the wild statements.**​  
“**[**Faith in the Possible**](https://reidhoffman.substack.com/p/faith-in-the-possible?mc_cid=034a07274e)**.”** This is the first article on [Reid Hoffman](https://tim.blog/2015/08/31/the-oracle-of-silicon-valley-reid-hoffman-plus-michael-mccullough/)’s new Substack _Theory of the Game_. This piece has a good fine-slicing of the religion of techno-optimism, which is reframed as _creation_. His description of the various religious factions is very good, and I hadn’t seen it put so succinctly before. One important footnote: read the comments. I’m sharing this article for the thought-provoking comments as much as I am for the piece itself. Some of them provide alternative lenses and more critical views of startups as engines of progress.

bullets.section: Short video that’s making me safer
bullets.title: Rory Sutherland explains how one tiny detail on your dashboard could completely transform how we think about speed and safety
bullets.note: [Rory Sutherland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rory_Sutherland_(advertising_executive)) is vice chairman of Ogilvy. This clip comes from his talk “[Alchemy: The Surprising Power of Ideas That Don’t Make Sense](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lhlS-Wds02M)” (the clip starts at [18:11](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lhlS-Wds02M&t=1091s)). For another take on this concept, check out [Derek Sivers’ hilarious story](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=amS0u15AL14) about biking and bird poop. Hat tip to drummer extraordinaire [Dave Elitch](https://daveelitch.com/) for putting this on my radar.

bullets.title: Ocular Glymphatic System: Its Modulation and Role in Intraocular Tumors
bullets.creator: Dr
bullets.note: Jasmine H. Francis and Dr. David H. Abramson. The glymphatic system is worth getting familiar with. Excerpt: “The glymphatic system is a glial-based perivascular network that clears metabolic waste from the central nervous system (CNS), and its dysfunction is related to neurodegenerative disease.” New therapies for enhancing CNS glymphatic flow are discussed in this piece.
